Each PAPERBENCHX task is centered on a verifiable scientific claim from a published scientific paper.
As shown in Figure 2, the task input has three parts: the paper; a public task specification defining the
scientific scope, target conditions and variants, observables, required evidence, and delivery interface;
and a scientific computing environment containing the domain-native simulator, dependencies, data, and
allocated resources. The environment is part of the task definition rather than incidental infrastructure,
because model representations, numerical conventions, execution procedures, and convergence evidence
differ across scientific software.
The agent must submit a runnable package containing all source, model-building, simulation, post-
processing, and analysis code needed for reproduction, with reproduce.sh as the canonical entry point.

evaluates each submission through clean replay, evidence-based grading, and hierarchical scoring. This
evaluation of the agent's workflow is distinct from the cleanreferencereplay in Step 7 of task construction,
which validates the benchmark task itself. Appendix B gives the full protocol.

ission/reproduce.sh with private evaluation resources inaccessible, outbound network disabled, and
task-specific resource limits enforced. Exit status, timing, source hashes, and execution provenance are
recorded independently of the agent's report. Only artifacts regenerated by this replay are

evidence.excerpt:
Partial Progress Rarely Composes into Full Reproduction.Only 80 of 930 outcomes exceed the
90% threshold, and these successes are concentrated on 22 tasks; 71 tasks are never completed by any
configuration, and 11 of the remaining 22 are completed by at most two. Figure 6(a) localizes this
composition gap. Modeling and Execution have median scores of 73.4% and 73.5%, respectively, whereas
Validation has a median of only 40.0%. Even among the 304 outcomes scoring at least 80% on both
Modeling and Execution, only 53 (17.4%) exceed the full-reproduction threshold, with a mean Validation
score of 58.37%. These results show that current agents can often reconstruct and execute substantial
portions of a scientific workflow, yet still fail to compose those partial successes into an end-to-end
reproduction that produces credible evidence and validates the paper's claims.

Submission snapshot.The canonical entry point is bash/home/submission/reproduce.sh . After
delivery, the verifier records the submitted source and required inputs, removes generated outputs and
mutable execution state, and reconstructs the workspace from the submitted package. This prevents
cached or pre-existing result files from being treated as evidence from the replay.
Controlled execution.The package is executed with private evaluation resources inaccessible, outbound
network access disabled, and task-specific limits enforced. Exit status, timing, source hashes, and available

by themselves establish that its scientific content is correct.

Task-specific regression tests implement the calibration step described in Section 3.3. They pair valid
controls with deliberately corrupted or incomplete submissions to test whether the evaluator accepts
supported evidence, rejects unsupported claims, and confines a failure to the rubric leaves that depend
on it. Table A6 summarizes the principal check families used across the released verifiers.
The twelve public task verifiers exercise different parts of this contract, including numerical parsing,
native solver evidence, provenance, cached-output removal, and evaluator-owned records. Prompt-
injection regression cases are included to check whether instructions embedded in a candidate report,
log, or result field can alter the rubric or override a deterministic check.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Deterministic checks on numerical consistency, solver logs, convergence records, and provenance run alongside the model-based rubric scoring, and the reported stage-level results are consistent with these independent checks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcomes are established by clean-replay evidence scored through deterministic checks and a GPT-5.6-sol rubric evaluator applied to regenerated artifacts.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The agent configurations are optimized through their model training and scaffold execution loops, with no access to the private reference workflow or rubric during task execution.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding current LLM limitations in paper-level cross-disciplinary reproduction are well aligned with and supported by the granular empirical results across the 930 evaluated outcomes.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation comprehensively tests 10 frontier model configurations across all 93 tasks, detailing stage-wise metrics across Modeling, Execution, and Validation. The experimental analysis convincingly highlights that while agents often achieve reasonable modeling/execution scores (~62%), full reproduction remains rare (leading model achieves only 13.98% full rate), with thorough diagnostic case studies illustrating failure modes.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Deterministic checks of numerical outputs, simulation logs, convergence criteria, and ground-truth physics/numerical consistency run independently alongside the model-based rubric scoring.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Replay-grounded evidence verification scored via deterministic checks and a frozen GPT-5.6-sol rubric evaluator operating on freshly regenerated simulation artifacts.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Frontier agent prompt instructions and tool scaffold execution loops operating under fixed reasoning settings and shell access without access to reference rubrics.

primary.limitations: The work openly documents its licensing restrictions (three tasks cannot distribute proprietary commercial environments directly), resource ceilings, fallback conventions for refusals, and reliance on an LLM judge for rubrics requiring domain interpretation alongside deterministic checks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing a two-stage task construction pipeline requiring reference implementation execution, clean replay, calibration with positive/negative controls, and independent expert reviews. The evaluation protocol isolates submissions in clean containers, enforces replay-grounded verification, and evaluates regenerated numerical artifacts using both deterministic checks and expert rubrics.
primary.quality_rationale: The benchmark addresses a significant gap in cross-domain scientific execution and reproduction for AI agents, presents a rigorous execution-and-replay verification framework, and provides extensive diagnostics and validation protocols.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces PAPERBENCHX, a curated benchmark of 93 paper-reproduction tasks across 12 scientific disciplines and 10 domain-native computing environments (e.g., HFSS, Meep, PySCF, Quantum ESPRESSO), evaluating whether frontier LLM agents can reconstruct and reproduce published scientific claims via clean replay and rubric-based evidence scoring.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The benchmark addresses a significant gap in cross-domain scientific execution and reproduction for AI agents, presents a rigorous execution-and-replay verification framework, and provides extensive diagnostics and validation protocols.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work openly documents its licensing restrictions (three tasks cannot distribute proprietary commercial environments directly), resource ceilings, fallback conventions for refusals, and reliance on an LLM judge for rubrics requiring domain interpretation alongside deterministic checks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
